daily_reality.summary: Hospitalists are physicians specializing in the care of hospitalized patients. They manage admissions, discharges, and coordinate inpatient care. Most common schedule is 7-on/7-off with 12-hour shifts. They face growing patient complexity and volume as the field expands rapidly.
typical_tasks: Conduct morning rounds on assigned patients (15-20 patients typical)
Admit new patients from emergency department
Order and interpret diagnostic tests and imaging
Coordinate care with specialists, nurses, and case managers
Perform bedside procedures (central lines, lumbar punctures, paracentesis)
Document encounters in EHR (admission notes, progress notes, discharge summaries)
Participate in rapid response and code blue teams
Conduct discharge planning and medication reconciliation
Communicate with families about patient status and care plans
Participate in quality improvement and utilization review committees

deadlines.signout: End of each shift for handoff

daily_reality.seasonality: Winter flu/respiratory season (Nov-March) dramatically increases admissions. Holiday periods create staffing challenges. Summer may see reduced elective admissions.

regulatory.summary: Requires MD/DO, completed Internal Medicine residency, board certification. Hospital credentialing and privileging required. Governed by CMS Conditions of Participation, Joint Commission standards, and state medical practice acts.

key_laws.name: CMS Conditions of Participation
key_laws.description: Federal requirements for hospitals participating in Medicare/Medicaid

key_laws.name: Joint Commission Standards
key_laws.description: Hospital accreditation standards affecting medical staff practice

key_laws.name: State Medical Practice Acts
key_laws.description: State-level physician licensing and practice regulation

key_laws.name: EMTALA
key_laws.description: Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act — requires emergency screening and stabilization

certifications: ABIM Board Certification in Internal Medicine
Focused Practice in Hospital Medicine (FPHM) — recognition from ABIM

regulatory.penalties: Malpractice liability, hospital peer review actions, medical board discipline, CMS penalties for quality metrics non-compliance.

tools.summary: EHR systems (Epic, Cerner) are the primary daily tool. Point-of-care ultrasound, clinical decision support, and communication platforms are increasingly important.

primary_tools.name: Epic / Oracle Health (Cerner)
primary_tools.description: EHR for documentation, orders, medication management

primary_tools.name: POCUS (Point-of-Care Ultrasound)
primary_tools.description: Bedside diagnostic imaging for rapid assessment

terminology.summary: Hospital medicine terminology blends general medical terms with hospital-specific workflow and quality terminology.

terms.rounding: Systematic patient review and bedside assessment
terms.signout/handoff: Transfer of patient care responsibility between shifts
terms.boarder: Patient waiting in ED for an inpatient bed
terms.LOS: Length of Stay — key hospital quality metric
terms.readmission: Patient returning to hospital within 30 days of discharge
terms.RRT: Rapid Response Team — for deteriorating patients
terms.throughput: Patient flow efficiency through admission-discharge cycle
terms.discharge planning: Coordinated preparation for safe patient release
terms.NPO: Nothing by mouth — pre-procedure dietary restriction
terms.census: Number of patients assigned to a hospitalist
terms.disposition: Decision about next level of care for patient
terms.SNF: Skilled Nursing Facility — common discharge destination

career_psychology.summary: Fast-growing specialty with average salary $265K-$280K. 7-on/7-off schedule offers blocks of time off but grueling on-weeks. Burnout is significant concern due to high patient loads and 12-hour shifts. 26% projected growth by 2030.
career_path: Chief Medical Officer / VP of Medical Affairs
fears: Medical error affecting critically ill patient
Burnout from 12-hour shifts and high census
Malpractice lawsuit from complex inpatient care
Losing work-life balance due to demanding schedule
Compassion fatigue from high-acuity patient care
motivation: Direct impact on acutely ill patients' outcomes
Blocks of time off (7 days on / 7 days off)
Intellectual challenge of managing complex cases
Strong job market and career security
burnout_factors: Heavy patient census (15-20+ patients per shift)
Growing complexity and acuity of hospitalized patients

community.summary: Society of Hospital Medicine (SHM) is the primary professional organization. Rapidly growing specialty with strong community identity and advocacy.

associations.name: Society of Hospital Medicine (SHM)
associations.description: Primary professional society, 20,000+ members, advocacy, education

conferences: SHM State of Hospital Medicine Report

market.summary: One of the fastest-growing medical specialties with 26% projected growth by 2030. Average salary $265K-$280K. Driven by aging population, hospital efficiency demands, and shift toward employed physician models.
top_employers: Hospitalist management groups (Sound Physicians, TeamHealth, Envision)
market_trends: 26% projected growth making it fastest-growing medical specialty
Aging population driving increased inpatient volume
Shift from private practice model to employed hospitalist model
Co-management with surgical services expanding scope
Telemedicine integration for rural hospital coverage
